title: Old house history project

paragraphs.text: Part three.
You will hear a history student asking her tutor about techniques for tracing the history of an old house.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-five.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-five.
Thanks for agreeing to see me at such short notice, Dr. Hughes.
That's all right. What can I do to help?

Well, we're just starting our year two history project, and we'd like to do it on the history of my uncle's house in our village. There isn't much information on it, and he wants to find out more. You know, how old it is exactly, who lived in it and so on. Can you give us some advice on how to go about researching it? And we also wondered if you could give us some advice on how to actually structure the project write-up.

Well, I'll see what I can do. Uh, first of all, I think it's a very good topic for your project. House detective work can yield a lot of fascinating incidental information. Uh, for example, I think you should incorporate into your project any village history which seems to have a bearing on your project.
Yes, of course.
So where to start? Um, approximately how old is the house?
My uncle thinks two hundred and fifty years, but he's really interested in getting a more exact date.
Well, the first thing you need to get is the deeds, the documents which accompany the house sale. These should tell you the previous owners.
Mm-hmm. And will they show the age?
Mm, possibly not. You should bear in mind that deeds are often incomplete.
Mm.
You need to do a lot more work. My advice is to start by spending a bit of time looking at the house as a whole, trying to divine what the ground plan is.
Right.

Yes. Uh, it's a very good starting point for establishing the general date. Right. And once you've got that, the next thing is to visit the local library, and what you need to consult there are large-scale maps from the time you think the house was built. You can see at what date the house first appears.
Okay. Right.
And then it's worth looking into the house itself.
Mm-hmm.
Although you can never be sure that they are original, it is very fruitful to look at and sketch the fireplaces.
Yes. There are two or three large ones in the house. They're very distinctive.
Right. As I say, make a drawing of them and then look them up in a specialist book.
Yes.
And do the same for the staircases.
Okay. That'll be no problem. One of the group is a good artist.
Very useful.
Now, tell me, is there a wooden frame to the building?
Yes. It has lots of exposed wooden beams.
Well, there is something very special that you could do if you were interested in getting an extremely precise dating.
What's that?
If your uncle gave permission, you could take a small sample of the wood and discover the date by examining tree rings.
Really? Would that work?
Yes. It's a well-established procedure.
Could we do it at the university?
I think it could be arranged, yes.
That'd be brilliant. If we can manage it, that is.
Well, keep that in mind.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-six to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-six to thirty.
So can I also ask you about the project write-up?
Fine. Well, I always advise my students to have four main sections.
Mm-hmm.
The first section, which I think helps you a great deal with the rest, is reasons for choosing the topic.
Right. Yes. We've already made some notes on that.
Then the research process, including a description of any problems. Be honest about them.
Yes, of course. Knowing us, there'll be plenty.
There always are.
And then summary of findings. There'll probably be two main subsections there as well. Age.
Oh, right. Yes. And?
And the other subsection, I suppose you'd call occupancy.
Yes. Okay.
And the fourth and final section you should make unanswered questions.
There'll be a lot of those, I imagine.
You can work on them for your master's thesis.
Of course. Yes.
Well, thank you very much, Dr. Hughes.
You're welcome. Let me know how it's all going.
I certainly will.
That is the end of part three. You now have one minute to check your answers to part three.
